title: System / LAN administrator self-check
intro: Privileged operations, patching, backup, and Tier 3 monitoring.

choices: Knowing which powerful accounts exist, why, and who can use them.
A list of favourite passwords in a shared spreadsheet.
Replacing change control.
Publishing admin names on the intranet homepage.
questions.rationale: You cannot review what you have not listed. Pair the inventory with least privilege.

questions.prompt: For a Tier 2 system, how often does App C expect an independent privileged-account check?
choices: At least every six months.
Every five years.
Only after an incident becomes public.
Never, if the same admin reviews their own logins.
questions.rationale: App C §11: an independent party checks privileged use at least every six months. Tier 3 inherits this.

questions.prompt: A known vulnerability has a patch. App C’s usual timing is:
choices: As soon as possible, typically within a month. If it slips, tell the DITSO and keep updating them monthly until it is fixed.
Whenever the next hardware refresh happens.
Only if a newspaper asks.
Within one month, with no need to tell anyone if you miss it.
questions.rationale: App C §14 requires a documented risk view and DITSO visibility when mitigation exceeds a month.

questions.prompt: Tier 2 backup under App C includes:
choices: Local and off-site copies, with the off-site copy kept somewhere secure and remote from the equipment.
One copy on the same disk array.
A screenshot of the backup software.
Backups only after a disaster.
questions.rationale: App C §14 requires local and off-site backup for Tier 2, inherited by Tier 3.

questions.prompt: End-of-support software on a Tier 2 system needs:
choices: A migration plan at least six months before end of support, and the security measures in place by that date.
A note that you will look at it someday.
Nothing, if the vendor still answers email.
An immediate public disclosure of the version.
questions.rationale: That is the App C §14 end-of-support expectation.

questions.prompt: Tier 3 monitoring, beyond the Tier 2 operations controls, means:
choices: 24×7 security surveillance that can correlate multiple sources, of a SIEM class.
A daily glance at one antivirus console.
Monitoring only during office hours.
Disabling logs to save disk.
questions.rationale: App C §14 Tier 3 row: 24×7 monitoring and SIEM-class correlation. Tier 2 controls still apply as well.
